Computing the first derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(x) & ={(4{x}^{2}\sqrt{x}-2x+7)}^{′} \\  & ={(4{x}^{5/2}-2x+7)}^{′} \\  & =4(\frac{5}{2}){x}^{3/2}-2+0 \\  & =10{x}^{3/2}-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the second derivative, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{″}(x) & ={(10{x}^{3/2}-2)}^{′} \\  & =10(\frac{3}{2}){x}^{1/2}-0 \\  & =15{x}^{1/2} \\  & =15\sqrt{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, evaluating the second derivative at $x=4$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{″}(4) & =15\sqrt{4} \\  & =15(2) \\  & =30.\end{aligned}
$$
